```{r rename columns}

clean_names <- function(name) {
  
  # Special handling for "Please indicate how often..." format
  if (grepl("please indicate how often you have experienced the following over the last three months:", tolower(name))) {
    name <- sub(".*- ", "", name)
  }
  
  # Then apply standard cleaning
  name %>%
    tolower() %>%
    gsub("please ", "", .) %>%
    gsub("what is your ", "", .) %>%
    gsub("how often have you felt ", "", .) %>%
    gsub("how often ", "", .) %>%
    gsub("do you feel that ", "", .) %>%
    gsub("please describe ", "", .) %>%
    gsub("please state ", "", .) %>%
    gsub("\\?", "", .) %>%
    gsub(":", "", .) %>%
    gsub(" in years", "", .) %>%
    gsub(" over the last three months", "", .) %>%
    # Additional cleaning for specific columns
    gsub("your coping mechanisms for stress", "coping_mechanisms", .) %>%
    gsub("you are getting enough support from your university", "university_support", .) %>%
    gsub("your coping mechanisms help to manage or relieve stress successfully", "coping_effective", .) %>%
    # Final standardization
    gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "_", .) %>%
    gsub("^_+|_+$", "", .) %>%
    gsub("_+", "_", .)
}
# Apply cleaning
original_names <- colnames(uk_student_data)
colnames(uk_student_data) <- sapply(original_names, clean_names)

cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("COLUMN NAME MAPPINGS\n")
cat("========================================\n")
cat("Showing all column transformations:\n\n")

# Create a nice table format
mapping_df <- data.frame(
  Original = original_names,
  Cleaned = colnames(uk_student_data),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Print with better formatting
for (i in 1:nrow(mapping_df)) {
  cat(sprintf("%2d. %-70s → %s\n", 
              i, 
              substr(mapping_df$Original[i], 1, 70),  # Truncate if too long
              mapping_df$Cleaned[i]))
}

cat("\n========================================\n")
```

```{r linkert scale mapping }

# =============================================================================
# STEP 3: IDENTIFY AND CONVERT LIKERT SCALES
# =============================================================================

# Likert scale mapping
likert_map <- c(
  "Never" = 1,
  "Almost never" = 2,
  "Sometimes" = 3,
  "Fairly often" = 4,
  "Very often" = 5
)

cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("IDENTIFYING LIKERT SCALE COLUMNS\n")
cat("========================================\n")

# Identify Likert columns
likert_values <- c("Never", "Almost never", "Sometimes", "Fairly often", "Very often")
likert_cols <- c()

for (col in colnames(uk_student_data)) {
  # Check if column is character type
  if (is.character(uk_student_data[[col]])) {
    # Get unique non-NA values
    unique_vals <- unique(uk_student_data[[col]][!is.na(uk_student_data[[col]])])
    
    # Check if any Likert values present
    if (any(unique_vals %in% likert_values)) {
      likert_cols <- c(likert_cols, col)
      cat(sprintf("  ✓ Found Likert column: %s\n", col))
    }
  }
}

cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("LIKERT SCALE COLUMNS SUMMARY\n")
cat("========================================\n")
cat("Total Likert columns found:", length(likert_cols), "\n\n")

if (length(likert_cols) > 0) {
  cat("Columns to be converted:\n")
  print(likert_cols)
  
  cat("\n========================================\n")
  cat("CONVERTING LIKERT SCALES TO NUMERIC\n")
  cat("========================================\n")
  
  # Convert Likert to numeric
  for (col in likert_cols) {
    # Show before conversion
    cat(sprintf("\nConverting: %s\n", col))
    cat("  Before: ")
    print(table(uk_student_data[[col]], useNA = "ifany"))
    
    # Convert
    uk_student_data[[col]] <- likert_map[trimws(uk_student_data[[col]])]
    
    # Show after conversion
    cat("  After: ")
    print(summary(uk_student_data[[col]]))
  }
  
  cat("\n✓ All Likert scale conversions complete.\n")
} else {
  cat("⚠ WARNING: No Likert scale columns found!\n")
  cat("Please check your data format.\n")
}
```

```{r handling missing values}

cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("MISSING DATA SUMMARY\n")
cat("========================================\n")

missing_summary <- data.frame(
  column = colnames(uk_student_data),
  missing_count = colSums(is.na(uk_student_data)),
  missing_pct = round(colSums(is.na(uk_student_data)) / nrow(uk_student_data) * 100, 2)
) %>%
  filter(missing_count > 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(missing_pct))

if (nrow(missing_summary) > 0) {
  print(head(missing_summary, 10))
  
  # Impute numerical columns with mean
  for (col in colnames(uk_student_data)) {
    if (is.numeric(uk_student_data[[col]]) && any(is.na(uk_student_data[[col]]))) {
      mean_val <- mean(uk_student_data[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
      uk_student_data[[col]][is.na(uk_student_data[[col]])] <- mean_val
      cat(sprintf("✓ Imputed '%s' with mean: %.2f\n", col, mean_val))
    }
  }
  
  # Replace NA in text columns with "No response"
  for (col in colnames(uk_student_data)) {
    if (is.character(uk_student_data[[col]])) {
      uk_student_data[[col]][is.na(uk_student_data[[col]]) | uk_student_data[[col]] == ""] <- "No response"
    }
  }
} else {
  cat("No missing values found.\n")
}
```

```{r create stress level categories }

# =============================================================================
# STEP 5: CREATE STRESS LEVEL CATEGORIES
# =============================================================================

# First, find the stress column
stress_col <- grep("stress|felt_stress|how_often_have_you_felt", colnames(uk_student_data), 
                   ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)[1]

if (is.na(stress_col)) {
  cat("\n⚠ WARNING: Could not find stress column. Please specify manually.\n")
  cat("Available columns:\n")
  print(colnames(uk_student_data))
  stop("Please specify the stress column manually.")
} else {
  cat(sprintf("\n✓ Using stress column: %s\n", stress_col))
  
  # Check current values
  cat("\n========================================\n")
  cat("CURRENT STRESS COLUMN VALUES\n")
  cat("========================================\n")
  print(table(uk_student_data[[stress_col]], useNA = "ifany"))
  
  # Define mapping for this specific scale (4-point scale)
  # Question: "How often have you felt stressed over the last three months?"
  # Scale interpretation: Higher value = More stress
  stress_mapping <- c(
    "To a small extent" = 1,    # Least stressed
    "Somewhat" = 2,              # Moderately stressed
    "To a large extent" = 3,     # Very stressed
    "Completely" = 4             # Most stressed
  )
  
  cat("\nApplying stress scale mapping (1-4):\n")
  print(stress_mapping)
  
  # Convert to numeric
  uk_student_data[[stress_col]] <- stress_mapping[trimws(uk_student_data[[stress_col]])]
  
  cat("\n========================================\n")
  cat("CONVERTED STRESS VALUES\n")
  cat("========================================\n")
  print(summary(uk_student_data[[stress_col]]))
  print(table(uk_student_data[[stress_col]], useNA = "ifany"))
  
  # Check for any NAs (unmapped values)
  na_count <- sum(is.na(uk_student_data[[stress_col]]))
  if (na_count > 0) {
    cat(sprintf("\n⚠ WARNING: %d values could not be mapped. Check for typos or different values.\n", na_count))
    cat("Unique unmapped values:\n")
    unmapped <- uk_student_data[[stress_col]][is.na(uk_student_data[[stress_col]])]
    if (length(unmapped) > 0) {
      print(unique(unmapped))
    }
  }
  
  # Create stress level categories for 4-point scale
  # Adjusted breaks for 1-4 scale:
  # Low: 1-1.67 (score 1)
  # Medium: 1.68-2.67 (score 2)  
  # High: 2.68-4 (scores 3-4)
  uk_student_data$stress_level <- cut(
    uk_student_data[[stress_col]],
    breaks = c(0, 1.67, 2.67, 4),
    labels = c("Low", "Medium", "High"),
    include.lowest = TRUE,
    right = TRUE
  )
  
  # Alternative: Equal intervals (simpler)
  # uk_student_data$stress_level <- cut(
  #   uk_student_data[[stress_col]],
  #   breaks = c(0, 1.5, 2.5, 4),
  #   labels = c("Low", "Medium", "High"),
  #   include.lowest = TRUE
  # )
  
  cat("\n========================================\n")
  cat("STRESS LEVEL DISTRIBUTION\n")
  cat("========================================\n")
  cat("Categorization:\n")
  cat("  Low:    1.00 - 1.67 (To a small extent)\n")
  cat("  Medium: 1.68 - 2.67 (Somewhat)\n")
  cat("  High:   2.68 - 4.00 (To a large extent, Completely)\n\n")
  
  stress_table <- table(uk_student_data$stress_level, useNA = "ifany")
  stress_pct <- prop.table(stress_table) * 100
  
  for (level in names(stress_table)) {
    cat(sprintf("  %s: %d (%.1f%%)\n", level, stress_table[level], stress_pct[level]))
  }
  
  # Cross-tabulation to verify mapping
  cat("\n========================================\n")
  cat("CROSS-TAB: Original Score vs Category\n")
  cat("========================================\n")
  cross_tab <- table(
    Original_Score = uk_student_data[[stress_col]], 
    Stress_Level = uk_student_data$stress_level,
    useNA = "ifany"
  )
  print(cross_tab)
  
  # Plot stress distribution
  p_stress <- ggplot(uk_student_data, aes(x = stress_level, fill = stress_level)) +
    geom_bar() +
    geom_text(stat = 'count', aes(label = after_stat(count)), vjust = -0.5, size = 5) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Low" = "#2ECC71", "Medium" = "#F39C12", "High" = "#E74C3C")) +
    labs(title = "Stress Level Distribution", 
         subtitle = paste("Based on:", stress_col, "(4-point scale)"),
         x = "Stress Level", y = "Count") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "none",
          text = element_text(size = 12))
  
  print(p_stress)
  
  # Additional plot: Distribution of numeric scores
  p_numeric <- ggplot(uk_student_data, aes(x = factor(uk_student_data[[stress_col]]))) +
    geom_bar(fill = "#3498DB") +
    geom_text(stat = 'count', aes(label = after_stat(count)), vjust = -0.5, size = 5) +
    labs(title = "Distribution of Stress Scores",
         subtitle = "1 = To a small extent, 2 = Somewhat, 3 = To a large extent, 4 = Completely",
         x = "Stress Score", y = "Count") +
    theme_minimal()
  
  print(p_numeric)
  
  cat("\n✓ Stress level categorization complete.\n")
}
```

```{r corr analysis}

# Combine all features
all_features <- unique(c(symptom_cols, stressor_cols))
all_features <- all_features[all_features %in% colnames(uk_student_data)]

# Add stress column
cor_cols <- c(stress_col, all_features)

# Calculate correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- cor(uk_student_data[, cor_cols], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# Extract correlations with stress
stress_cors <- data.frame(
  feature = rownames(cor_matrix)[-1],  # Exclude stress itself
  correlation = cor_matrix[-1, stress_col]
) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(correlation)))

cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("TOP 15 FEATURES CORRELATED WITH STRESS\n")
cat("========================================\n")
print(head(stress_cors, 15))

# Plot top correlations
ggplot(head(stress_cors, 15), aes(x = reorder(feature, correlation), y = correlation)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", aes(fill = correlation > 0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#E74C3C", "FALSE" = "#3498DB")) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Top 15 Features Correlated with Stress",
       x = "Feature", y = "Correlation Coefficient") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r NLP text analysis}
library(tokenizers)  
# Identify coping mechanism column
coping_col <- grep("coping", colnames(uk_student_data), ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)[1]

if (is.na(coping_col)) {
  cat("\n⚠ WARNING: Could not find coping mechanism column.\n")
} else {
  cat(sprintf("\n✓ Using coping column: %s\n", coping_col))
}  
  # Extract text (exclude "No response")
  coping_text <- uk_student_data[[coping_col]]
  coping_text_clean <- coping_text[coping_text != "No response" & coping_text != ""]
  
  cat("\n========================================\n")
  cat("COPING MECHANISM TEXT SUMMARY\n")
  cat("========================================\n")
  cat("Total responses:", length(coping_text), "\n")
  cat("Valid responses:", length(coping_text_clean), "\n")
  cat("\nSample responses:\n")
  print(head(coping_text_clean, 3))


  # Text preprocessing
  corpus <- Corpus(VectorSource(coping_text_clean))
  corpus_clean <- corpus %>%
    tm_map(content_transformer(tolower)) %>%
    tm_map(removePunctuation) %>%
    tm_map(removeNumbers) %>%
    tm_map(stripWhitespace) %>%
    tm_map(removeWords, stopwords("english")) %>%
    tm_map(removeWords, c("etc", "also", "just", "can", "get", "try", "make"))
  
  # Create DTM
  dtm <- DocumentTermMatrix(corpus_clean)
  dtm_matrix <- as.matrix(dtm)
  
  # Term frequencies
  term_freq <- sort(colSums(dtm_matrix), decreasing = TRUE)
  term_df <- data.frame(term = names(term_freq), frequency = term_freq)
  
  cat("\n========================================\n")
  cat("TOP 20 TERMS IN COPING MECHANISMS\n")
  cat("========================================\n")
  print(head(term_df, 20))
  
  # Word cloud
  #install.packages("wordcloud")
  #library(wordcloud)
  #wordcloud(words = term_df$term, 
            #freq = term_df$frequency,
            #min.freq = 2,
            #max.words = 100,
            #random.order = FALSE,
            #colors = brewer.pal(8, "Dark2"))
 # title("Coping Mechanisms Word Cloud")
  
  # Bar chart of top terms
  ggplot(head(term_df, 20), aes(x = reorder(term, frequency), y = frequency)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "#9B59B6") +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(title = "Top 20 Terms in Coping Mechanisms",
         x = "Term", y = "Frequency") +
    theme_minimal()
  
  # =============================================================================
  # STEP 10: CATEGORIZE COPING MECHANISMS
  # =============================================================================
  
  # Define categories
  coping_categories <- list(
    exercise = c("exercise", "gym", "workout", "running", "run", "jogging", "sports", 
                 "swimming", "cycling", "fitness", "walk", "walking"),
    social = c("friends", "family", "talking", "socializing", "hang", "hanging", "people"),
    meditation_relaxation = c("meditation", "meditate", "breathing", "breath", "relaxation", 
                             "relax", "mindfulness", "yoga"),
    entertainment = c("music", "movie", "movies", "tv", "watch", "watching", "netflix", 
                     "series", "film", "gaming", "game", "games"),
    hobbies = c("reading", "read", "book", "books", "hobby", "art", "drawing", "painting", 
                "guitar", "play", "playing"),
    nature = c("nature", "outdoor", "outdoors", "park", "garden", "outside", "hiking"),
    food_drink = c("eating", "eat", "food", "cooking", "cook", "tea", "coffee", "drink", "drinking"),
    sleep_rest = c("sleep", "sleeping", "nap", "rest", "resting", "bed"),
    therapy = c("therapy", "therapist", "counseling", "counsellor", "professional")
  )
  
  # Create binary variables for each category
  for (category in names(coping_categories)) {
    keywords <- coping_categories[[category]]
    pattern <- paste0("\\b(", paste(keywords, collapse = "|"), ")\\b")
    uk_student_data[[paste0("coping_", category)]] <- as.integer(
      grepl(pattern, tolower(uk_student_data[[coping_col]]))
    )
  }
  
  # Calculate frequencies
  coping_category_cols <- grep("^coping_", colnames(uk_student_data), value = TRUE)
  
  category_freq <- data.frame(
    category = gsub("coping_", "", coping_category_cols),
    count = sapply(coping_category_cols, function(col) sum(uk_student_data[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)),
    percentage = sapply(coping_category_cols, function(col) 
      round(sum(uk_student_data[[col]], na.rm = TRUE) / nrow(uk_student_data) * 100, 2))
  ) %>%
    arrange(desc(count))
  
  cat("\n========================================\n")
  cat("COPING MECHANISM CATEGORIES\n")
  cat("========================================\n")
  print(category_freq)
  
  # Plot categories
  ggplot(category_freq, aes(x = reorder(category, count), y = count)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "#1ABC9C") +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(count, " (", percentage, "%)")), hjust = -0.1) +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(title = "Coping Mechanism Categories",
         x = "Category", y = "Count") +
    theme_minimal() +
    expand_limits(y = max(category_freq$count) * 1.15)
```

```{r coping mechanism}
# =============================================================================
# STEP 10: CATEGORIZE COPING MECHANISMS
# =============================================================================

cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("CATEGORIZING COPING MECHANISMS\n")
cat("========================================\n")

# Check if coping column exists and has data
if (!exists("coping_col") || is.na(coping_col)) {
  cat("⚠ WARNING: Coping column not found. Skipping this step.\n")
} else if (all(is.na(uk_student_data[[coping_col]])) || 
           all(uk_student_data[[coping_col]] == "No response")) {
  cat("⚠ WARNING: No valid coping responses found. Skipping this step.\n")
} else {
  
  # Define categories
  coping_categories <- list(
    exercise = c("exercise", "gym", "workout", "running", "run", "jogging", "sports", 
                 "swimming", "cycling", "fitness", "walk", "walking"),
    social = c("friends", "family", "talking", "socializing", "hang", "hanging", "people"),
    meditation_relaxation = c("meditation", "meditate", "breathing", "breath", "relaxation", 
                             "relax", "mindfulness", "yoga"),
    entertainment = c("music", "movie", "movies", "tv", "watch", "watching", "netflix", 
                     "series", "film", "gaming", "game", "games"),
    hobbies = c("reading", "read", "book", "books", "hobby", "art", "drawing", "painting", 
                "guitar", "play", "playing"),
    nature = c("nature", "outdoor", "outdoors", "park", "garden", "outside", "hiking"),
    food_drink = c("eating", "eat", "food", "cooking", "cook", "tea", "coffee", "drink", "drinking"),
    sleep_rest = c("sleep", "sleeping", "nap", "rest", "resting", "bed"),
    therapy = c("therapy", "therapist", "counseling", "counsellor", "professional")
  )
  
  cat("\nCreating binary variables for each category...\n")
  
  # Create binary variables for each category
  for (category in names(coping_categories)) {
    keywords <- coping_categories[[category]]
    pattern <- paste0("\\b(", paste(keywords, collapse = "|"), ")\\b")
    
    # Create the column with explicit steps
    text_to_search <- uk_student_data[[coping_col]]
    text_to_search[is.na(text_to_search)] <- ""
    text_lower <- tolower(text_to_search)
    matches <- grepl(pattern, text_lower, perl = TRUE)
    
    uk_student_data[[paste0("coping_", category)]] <- as.integer(matches)
    
    cat(sprintf("  ✓ Created: coping_%s (matches: %d)\n", category, sum(matches)))
  }
  
  # Get coping category columns - EXCLUDE coping_effective
  coping_category_cols <- grep("^coping_", colnames(uk_student_data), value = TRUE)
  coping_category_cols <- coping_category_cols[coping_category_cols != "coping_effective"]
  
  cat("\n========================================\n")
  cat("COPING CATEGORY COLUMNS (for analysis)\n")
  cat("========================================\n")
  print(coping_category_cols)
  
  # Calculate frequencies
  cat("\n========================================\n")
  cat("CALCULATING FREQUENCIES\n")
  cat("========================================\n")
  
  category_freq <- data.frame(
    category = character(),
    count = numeric(),
    percentage = numeric(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  for (col in coping_category_cols) {
    cat_name <- gsub("coping_", "", col)
    count_val <- sum(uk_student_data[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
    pct_val <- round(count_val / nrow(uk_student_data) * 100, 2)
    
    category_freq <- rbind(category_freq, data.frame(
      category = cat_name,
      count = count_val,
      percentage = pct_val,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    ))
  }
  
  # Sort by count
  category_freq <- category_freq %>% arrange(desc(count))
  
  cat("\n========================================\n")
  cat("COPING MECHANISM CATEGORIES\n")
  cat("========================================\n")
  print(category_freq)
  
  # Only plot if there's data
  if (sum(category_freq$count) > 0) {
    # Plot categories
    p_coping_cat <- ggplot(category_freq, aes(x = reorder(category, count), y = count)) +
      geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "#1ABC9C") +
      geom_text(aes(label = paste0(count, " (", percentage, "%)")), 
                hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
      coord_flip() +
      labs(title = "Coping Mechanism Categories",
           subtitle = paste("Based on", nrow(uk_student_data), "responses"),
           x = "Category", y = "Count") +
      theme_minimal() +
      expand_limits(y = max(category_freq$count) * 1.15)
    
    print(p_coping_cat)
    
    cat("\n✓ Coping categorization complete.\n")
  } else {
    cat("\n⚠ WARNING: No coping mechanisms detected in any category.\n")
    cat("\nSample of actual coping text (first 5 non-'No response' values):\n")
    sample_text <- head(uk_student_data[[coping_col]][
      uk_student_data[[coping_col]] != "No response" & 
      !is.na(uk_student_data[[coping_col]])
    ], 5)
    for (i in seq_along(sample_text)) {
      cat(sprintf("%d. %s\n", i, sample_text[i]))
    }
  }
}
```


```{r}

cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("ANALYZING COPING EFFECTIVENESS\n")
cat("========================================\n")

# Identify effectiveness column
eff_col <- grep("help|manage|relieve|success|effective", colnames(uk_student_data), 
                ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)

# Filter to exclude any coping_ columns
eff_col <- eff_col[!grepl("^coping_", eff_col)]

if (length(eff_col) == 0) {
  cat("⚠ WARNING: Could not find effectiveness column.\n")
  cat("Available columns containing 'help', 'manage', 'relieve', etc.:\n")
  relevant_cols <- grep("coping|help|manage", colnames(uk_student_data), 
                       ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)
  print(relevant_cols)
} else {
  eff_col <- eff_col[1]  # Take first match
  cat(sprintf("✓ Using effectiveness column: %s\n", eff_col))
  
  # Check current values
  cat("\nEffectiveness responses:\n")
  print(table(uk_student_data[[eff_col]], useNA = "ifany"))
  
  # Standardize responses (lowercase, trim)
  uk_student_data[[eff_col]] <- tolower(trimws(uk_student_data[[eff_col]]))
  
  # Create binary effectiveness variable
  uk_student_data$coping_effective_binary <- ifelse(
    grepl("yes", uk_student_data[[eff_col]], ignore.case = TRUE), 1,
    ifelse(grepl("no", uk_student_data[[eff_col]], ignore.case = TRUE), 0, NA)
  )
  
  cat("\nEffectiveness binary conversion:\n")
  print(table(uk_student_data$coping_effective_binary, 
              uk_student_data[[eff_col]], useNA = "ifany"))
  
  # Calculate effectiveness by category
  cat("\n========================================\n")
  cat("EFFECTIVENESS BY COPING CATEGORY\n")
  cat("========================================\n")
  
  eff_by_cat <- data.frame(
    category = character(),
    total_using = numeric(),
    effective_count = numeric(),
    not_effective_count = numeric(),
    effectiveness_rate = numeric(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  for (col in coping_category_cols) {
    # Filter people using this coping mechanism
    using_this <- uk_student_data[uk_student_data[[col]] == 1, ]
    
    if (nrow(using_this) > 0) {
      total <- nrow(using_this)
      effective <- sum(using_this$coping_effective_binary == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
      not_effective <- sum(using_this$coping_effective_binary == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
      rate <- round(effective / total * 100, 2)
      
      eff_by_cat <- rbind(eff_by_cat, data.frame(
        category = gsub("coping_", "", col),
        total_using = total,
        effective_count = effective,
        not_effective_count = not_effective,
        effectiveness_rate = rate,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      ))
    }
  }
  
  # Sort by effectiveness rate
  eff_by_cat <- eff_by_cat %>% arrange(desc(effectiveness_rate))
  
  print(eff_by_cat)
  
  # Plot effectiveness (minimum 5 users)
  eff_filtered <- eff_by_cat %>% filter(total_using >= 5)
  
  if (nrow(eff_filtered) > 0) {
    p_effectiveness <- ggplot(eff_filtered, 
                             aes(x = reorder(category, effectiveness_rate), 
                                 y = effectiveness_rate)) +
      geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "#27AE60") +
      geom_text(aes(label = paste0(effectiveness_rate, "%\n(n=", total_using, ")")), 
                hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
      coord_flip() +
      labs(title = "Coping Mechanism Effectiveness",
           subtitle = "Categories with at least 5 users",
           x = "Coping Category", y = "Effectiveness Rate (%)") +
      theme_minimal() +
      expand_limits(y = 100)
    
    print(p_effectiveness)
  } else {
    cat("⚠ Not enough data for effectiveness visualization (need at least 5 users per category)\n")
  }
  
  cat("\n✓ Effectiveness analysis complete.\n")
}
```
